title: Statements
summary: One page for one month: what you sold, what the marketplace kept, what you paid and what you owe.

sections.title: What is a statement?
sections.intro: A statement is a monthly paper, like a bank statement. It lists your paid orders, the system commission, the returns and refunds, and the payments you made to the marketplace, and it ends with how much you owe.

blocks.title: Why you need it
items: You can check every taka of the month in one place.
You can print it or save it as a PDF and keep it for your records.
It helps you see what to pay the marketplace.
If you and the marketplace do not agree on a number, the statement is the proof.

blocks.title: How to
steps: Read the page from the top.
Press "Print" to print it or to save it as a PDF.

items.means: The big numbers at a glance: sales, system commission, refunds and what you keep.
Each paid order of the month: the order, the amount and its system commission.
Returns that were finished in the month, the refund amount and the system commission given back.
The payments you made to the marketplace this month.

items.term: Owed at the start of the month
items.means: What you owed on day one.
The new system commission of the month, after the part given back from returns.

items.term: Owed at the end of the month
items.means: What you owe at the end. This is the number to pay.

blocks.text: If a number is negative, the marketplace owes you. This happens when an order that was already paid for was returned.
If there is nothing in a month, the page says "No paid orders this month." or "No payments this month."
